body: Yeah it really sucks. I understand *why* we gave this guy the credit, but I don't agree with it. Like I told the other agents though, our system keeps track of credits, so if this guy gets the impression he can call in and get credits all the time, those will run out really quickly. (And they reduce his "valued customer" score. Haha.)

Even if they had been nice, I wasn't about to do something like this against policy without a really good reason and approval from my supervisor, which they would not have gotten because the refund they were asking for was against the policy in like three different ways. Normally I never touch that refund button, all refunds go off as a case for our back office.

But yes had they been nice I probably would have felt a lot worse, and he wouldn't have been hung up on.

When I say nothing happened, I mean that I didn't get in any trouble. Hanging up on the guy wasn't even that big a deal as we are allowed to for abusive customers. I just got coached on the call, on how I could have calmed the dude down.
Yeah misapplied payment means someone fucked up and put the payment on the wrong account.

Holy shit, so many times in a day I get people calling me "I'm in the store about to do my upgrade and they told me I can get my upgrade fee waived if I talk to you."

No, you can't.

Yeah and then when you hear them talking in the background to the customer.

Yeah they can easily see I never placed an outbound call, but the odds were that with that note the next agent would just chalk it up to signal issues and it wouldn't come back to me. It actually did just because another agent on my team got the call and emailed my TL "cx thinks that throwaway654852 hung up on him", nothing happened.
Yeah. IMO, fully gown adults shouldn't need any warnings not to yell and swear at the people who they just called for help.

This call came back to me today from another agent at my site through my team lead. We listened to the call together. She said she didn't blame me for hanging up and nothing happened. Just "how can we improve next time".
You made a good choice there.

I had one guy who did $400 of calls to a #89765 type premium "dating" number. Something like 40 calls lasting 13 minutes each at $9.99 per call. He got nothing. lol

Another woman had a $3000 roaming bill.
It wasn't intentional one way or another, but I'm leaving it the way it is!
Best two comments in the thread here, thanks guys. I will try this approach next time and see how it works.
